CategoryProfile.description: Category-specific part of a dataset profile: what a modeler must know about one kind of UBEM data before using it. There is one profile class per UBEM workflow role. The classes refine the per-category metadata table of an earlier taxonomy of open UBEM data: its free-text fields became typed fields with closed value lists, its "macroscopic" and "microscopic" energy data share EnergyProfile and differ in energy_data_scale, and its "comprehensive data lake" is a Catalog of profiles rather than a category.

metadata_standards.description: Metadata standards or schemas the publisher already uses (for example Brick, BuildingSync, DDI-Codebook, CityGML).

provides_concepts.description: Ids of the UBEM-Link concepts the dataset provides values for (its content at concept level).

representativeness.description: How the covered buildings relate to the building stock, which decides whether results generalize.

Convention.description: A rule the publisher applies to many variables at once, such as a naming pattern for imputation flags, a code that means "not applicable", or a unit used for all energy totals. Conventions are usually stated once in a user guide and never in the individual codebook entries, so a person or an AI system reading one entry cannot infer them; the profile states them explicitly.

applies_to.description: Which variables the convention applies to (a name pattern or a description).

applies_to_codes.description: Codes or code labels that must all occur in a variable's documented codes for the convention to apply (machine-readable scope by code list, for example Yes, No and Don't know for yes/no questions).

applies_to_pattern.description: Regular expression over variable names giving the variables a convention applies to (machine-readable scope).

applies_to_variables.description: Exact names of the variables a convention applies to (machine-readable scope).

convention_type.description: What the convention concerns, so that tools can apply it (missing codes, units, flags, keys).

example.description: One concrete example of the rule from the dataset.

missing_codes.description: Raw values that mean missing, not applicable, or suppressed.

rule.description: The convention, stated as a rule that can be applied without other context.

unit.description: QUDT unit CURIE, e.g. unit:FT2, unit:KiloBTU_IT, unit:KiloW-HR, unit:DEG_C.

unit_multiplier.description: Factor applied to raw values before the unit applies (e.g., 1000 for "thousand Btu").

UBEMConcept.description: A concept in the UBEM-Link vocabulary: a quantity or attribute that a UBEM workflow consumes or produces (for example floor area, principal building activity, dry-bulb temperature, annual electricity use). Concepts form a hierarchy through `broader` and point to equivalent terms in other standards.

broad_match.description: Term in another standard that is more general (SKOS broadMatch).

broader.description: The more general concept in the hierarchy (SKOS broader).

canonical_unit.description: SI (or SI-accepted) unit in which normalized values are expressed.

close_match.description: Term in another standard with nearly the same meaning (SKOS closeMatch).

concept_role.description: UBEM workflow role the concept belongs to.

definition.description: What the concept means, written so that a person or an AI system can apply it without other context.

entity.description: What the variable or concept describes (building, household, system, meter, region, ...).

exact_match.description: Term in another standard with the same meaning (SKOS exactMatch).

id.description: Stable lowercase identifier of the record (letters, digits, '_', '.', '-').

narrow_match.description: Term in another standard that is more specific (SKOS narrowMatch).

pref_label.description: Preferred human-readable label of the concept.

quantity_kind.description: QUDT quantity kind CURIE, e.g. quantitykind:Area.

related_match.description: Term in another standard that is associated but not equivalent (SKOS relatedMatch).

unit.description: QUDT unit CURIE, e.g. unit:FT2, unit:KiloBTU_IT, unit:KiloW-HR, unit:DEG_C.

unit_multiplier.description: Factor applied to raw values before the unit applies (e.g., 1000 for "thousand Btu").
